Notes.Text:
This update for python-tornado6 fixes the following issues:

- CVE-2024-14029: duplicate `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` headers are ignored, which allows for HTTP request smuggling
  (bsc#1284796).
- CVE-2026-103261: failure to limit the number of query string fields in `HTTPServerRequest.__init__` allows remote
  attackers to cause event-loop stalling (bsc#1283943).
- CVE-2026-103262: unbounded memory accumulation in `CurlAsyncHTTPClient` allows remote attackers to cause denial of
  service (bsc#1283961).
- CVE-2026-103263: `StaticFileHandler` follows symbolic links outside the static root and allows unauthorized users to
  gain read access to sensitive files (bsc#1283974).
- CVE-2026-115927: event loop blocking and excess memory use from chunked bodies with many small chunks allows for
  denial of service (bsc#1289051).
- CVE-2026-116577: quadratic CPU usage when parsing HTTP headers with line folding allows for denial of service
  (bsc#1289066).
- CVE-2026-116578: open redirect via crafted request paths in `RedirectHandler` URL templates allows for phishing
  attacks (bsc#1289059).

Vulnerabilities.Description: Tornado before 6.4.1 ignores duplicate Transfer-Encoding: chunked headers, treating requests as having no message body and parsing the chunked body as a subsequent request. Attackers can exploit this inconsistency when Tornado is deployed behind proxies to perform HTTP request smuggling, enabling access control bypass, cache poisoning, or connection desynchronization.

Vulnerabilities.Description: Tornado before 6.5.9 fails to limit the number of query string fields in HTTPServerRequest.__init__, allowing remote attackers to cause event-loop stalling by sending requests with thousands of query parameters. Attackers can send unauthenticated GET requests with unbounded query-string field counts to degrade response times for all clients sharing the same IOLoop.

Vulnerabilities.Description: Tornado versions before 6.5.9 contain an unbounded memory accumulation vulnerability in CurlAsyncHTTPClient that allows remote attackers to cause denial of service by sending a compressed response. Attackers can send a gzip-encoded decompression bomb that accumulates in memory without size limits, causing the application process to be killed by out-of-memory conditions.

Vulnerabilities.Description: Tornado before 6.5.9 contains a path traversal vulnerability in StaticFileHandler that follows symbolic links inside the static root without confirming the resolved target stays within it. When a symlink pointing outside the static directory exists inside it, unauthenticated attackers can request it to read files such as configuration files, private keys, and application secrets accessible to the process user.

Vulnerabilities.Description: Tornado is a Python web framework and asynchronous networking library. Prior to 6.6.0, Tornado decodes HTTP/1.1 chunked transfer encoding by processing body data that has already arrived without yielding to the event loop. A remote unauthenticated peer can send millions of one-byte chunks to monopolize the process event loop and stall every other connection served by that process, while lowering max_body_size only limits the duration of each request. For handlers that do not use @stream_request_body, retaining each chunk as a separate object can consume roughly twenty times the received body size, and SimpleAsyncHTTPClient has the same event-loop behavior when reading a response from a malicious server. This issue is fixed in version 6.6.0.

Vulnerabilities.Description: Tornado is a Python web framework and asynchronous networking library. Prior to 6.6, Tornado's HTTP header parser accepts obsolete line folding and repeatedly concatenates short continuation lines, causing quadratic CPU consumption on the IOLoop thread. An unauthenticated client can submit a header block containing many obsolete line-folding continuations before application code runs, blocking other connections served by the process. The cost grows with max_header_size, and only availability is affected. This issue is fixed in version 6.6.

Vulnerabilities.Description: Tornado is a Python web framework and asynchronous networking library. Prior to 6.6, tornado.web.RedirectHandler URL templates can place regex-capture substitutions where crafted request paths change the redirect scheme or network location. Affected placements include substitutions at the start of a path, directly after a fixed host, or at the beginning of the template, including protocol-relative, absolute, backslash, encoded, host-extension, and user-info variants interpreted by browsers as attacker-controlled destinations. Static templates and substitutions after a fixed host followed by a slash are not affected. An attacker can use the resulting open redirect on the application's domain for phishing. This issue is fixed in version 6.6.
